titleEn: El Niño threatens health, too – early warnings done right can save lives
titleZh: 厄尔尼诺也威胁健康：有效预警如何挽救生命
method: Machine reference translation with paragraph alignment; not manually certified.

paragraphs.en: As communities around the world shore up their infrastructure in anticipation of one of the most powerful El Niños on record in late 2026 and early 2027, they need to think about rising health risks, too – and include them in early weather warnings.
paragraphs.zh: 随着世界各地的社区预计2026年底和2027年初将出现有史以来最强大的厄尔尼诺现象之一，他们也需要考虑不断上升的健康风险，并将其纳入早期天气预警。

paragraphs.en: El Niño is part of a natural climate phenomenon that shifts global weather patterns for months at a time. During El Niño years, global temperatures tend to rise, triggering heat waves; normally dry regions can be hit with flooding rainfall; and normally wet regions often face droughts. All carry serious health risks.
paragraphs.zh: 厄尔尼诺现象是一种自然气候现象的一部分，它会在几个月内改变全球天气模式。在厄尔尼诺现象发生期间，全球气温往往会上升，引发热浪;通常干燥的地区可能会遭受洪水的袭击;通常潮湿的地区经常面临干旱。所有这些都带来严重的健康风险。

paragraphs.en: In southern Africa, for example, forecasters are warning of a rising risk of severe drought that could affect the 2026-27 growing season in key farming regions. At the same time, wetter-than-normal conditions in the Horn of Africa raise the risk of flooding and mosquito-borne disease outbreaks there.
paragraphs.zh: 例如，在南部非洲，天气预报员警告说，严重干旱的风险正在上升，这可能会影响2026-27年主要农业地区的生长季节。与此同时，非洲之角比正常情况更潮湿的条件增加了那里发生洪水和蚊媒疾病爆发的风险。

paragraphs.en: Dry conditions in Southeast Asia are already fueling wildfires and sending water supplies falling. October downpours in Chile triggered mudslides that left a mess for people to clean up in homes and yards.
paragraphs.zh: 东南亚的干旱状况已经加剧了野火，导致供水下降。智利10月的倾盆大雨引发了泥石流，人们在家中和院子里清理时留下了一片狼借。

paragraphs.en: In the United States, the South tends to be wetter than normal during El Niño years; drought is more likely in the Northern Plains; and storms can be fierce, particularly along the Pacific Coast.
paragraphs.zh: 在美国，南方在厄尔尼诺年往往比正常情况下更潮湿;北方平原更有可能发生干旱;风暴可能很猛烈，特别是沿着太平洋海岸。

paragraphs.en: As researchers in psychology, global health and Earth system science, we study how environmental disruptions affect people’s health and their ability to respond.
paragraphs.zh: 作为心理学，全球健康和地球系统科学的研究人员，我们研究环境破坏如何影响人们的健康及其应对能力。

paragraphs.en: To protect the population, communities need plans that keep care accessible and weather warnings that provide advice people can act on before, during and after a disaster.
paragraphs.zh: 为了保护民众，社区需要制定计划，使人们能够获得护理，并提供天气警报，以便人们在灾害发生之前、期间和之后采取行动。

paragraphs.en: When extreme weather becomes a health emergency
paragraphs.zh: 当极端天气成为健康紧急事件时

paragraphs.en: The health consequences of extreme weather events often extend beyond the immediate hazard.
paragraphs.zh: 极端天气事件的健康后果往往超出了直接危害。

paragraphs.en: For example, research has linked exposure to flooding, wildfire and ecosystem changes with elevated risks of illnesses, psychological distress and chronic stress.
paragraphs.zh: 例如，研究表明，洪水、野火和生态系统变化与疾病、心理困扰和慢性压力的风险增加有关。

paragraphs.en: Floodwater can lead to infections, such as hepatitis, cryptosporidium and fungal diseases, as well as longer-term health damage through exposure to harmful environmental microbes, chemicals and an increase in disease-carrying vectors such as mosquitoes.
paragraphs.zh: 洪水可导致感染，如肝炎，隐孢子虫和真菌疾病，以及通过接触有害的环境微生物，化学品和蚊子等携带疾病的媒介的增加而造成的长期健康损害。

paragraphs.en: Drought can lead to poor air quality and, in some places, malnutrition.
paragraphs.zh: 干旱可能导致空气质量差，在某些地方还可能导致营养不良。

paragraphs.en: Disasters can also keep people from getting essential healthcare, disrupt their livelihoods and displace them from their homes and social networks.
paragraphs.zh: 灾害还可能使人们无法获得基本的医疗保健，破坏他们的生计，使他们离开家园和社交网络。

paragraphs.en: The threat of a changing, potentially unsafe environment can also increase anticipatory, long-term distress. The World Health Organization identifies anxiety and post-traumatic stress as mental health consequences of extreme weather-related hazards. We believe mental health counseling services also belong in communities’ preparedness and recovery plans, not as an optional add-on after addressing physical needs.
paragraphs.zh: 一个不断变化的、潜在的不安全环境的威胁也会增加预期的、长期的痛苦。世界卫生组织将焦虑和创伤后压力确定为极端天气相关危害的心理健康后果。我们相信心理健康咨询服务也属于社区的准备和恢复计划，而不是在满足身体需求之后的可选附加服务。

paragraphs.en: Vulnerable populations face even higher risks
paragraphs.zh: 弱势群体面临的风险甚至更高

paragraphs.en: For people with existing illnesses or in areas far from medical care, extreme weather brings additional risks. These individuals and healthcare systems benefit from early warnings about El Niño’s disaster risks that help them prepare well in advance.
paragraphs.zh: 对于患有疾病或远离医疗保健地区的人来说，极端天气会带来额外的风险。这些人和医疗保健系统受益于厄尔尼诺灾害风险的早期预警，帮助他们提前做好准备。

paragraphs.en: At least 2.5 million Americans rely on in-home electricity-powered medical equipment, such as oxygen concentrators and ventilators, including nearly 78,000 who receive dialysis at home to help their kidneys function. When the power goes out or water is disrupted, they risk losing use of what may be life-sustaining equipment.
paragraphs.zh: 至少有250万美国人依赖家用电动医疗设备，如制氧机和呼吸机，其中近7.8万人在家中接受透析，以帮助他们的肾脏发挥功能。当停电或供水中断时，他们可能会失去使用这些可能是维持生命的设备。

paragraphs.en: Distance compounds these risks. Many communities around the world don’t have local clinics. Rural Americans live an average of 10.5 miles (17 kilometers) from the nearest hospital, and for 1 in 4 rural residents, the trip takes more than 30 minutes on average – before a single road floods. During Hurricane Harvey in 2017, flooding limited access to Houston’s second-busiest hospital for five days. The most extensive disruptions were in lower-income and minority neighborhoods.
paragraphs.zh: 距离加剧了这些风险。世界各地的许多社区没有当地的诊所。美国农村地区的平均居住距离为10.5英里（17公里）距离最近的医院，对于四分之一的农村居民来说，行程平均需要30多分钟-在一条道路被洪水淹没之前。2017年哈维飓风期间，洪水使休斯顿第二繁忙的医院的交通中断了五天。最大的中断发生在低收入和少数民族社区。

paragraphs.en: With advanced warnings, community organizations and healthcare providers preparing for El Niño can contact people with health vulnerabilities early to arrange backup power supplies and help them prepare so they know what to do when disasters do strike.
paragraphs.zh: 有了预先警告，社区组织和医疗保健提供者可以及早联系健康脆弱的人，安排备用电源，帮助他们做好准备，以便他们知道灾害发生时该怎么做。

paragraphs.en: How to turn forecasts into protection
paragraphs.zh: 如何将预测转化为保护

paragraphs.en: A good weather warning doesn’t just name the threat. It also provides information that residents can act on to stay safe through the disaster and the recovery afterward.
paragraphs.zh: 一个好的天气预警不仅仅是说出威胁的名称，它还提供了居民可以采取行动的信息，以便在灾难发生和灾后恢复期间保持安全。

paragraphs.en: Communities do not need to wait until a disaster is building to begin preparing. Existing community emergency plans, patient outreach programs and social networks provide a starting point for steps that help.
paragraphs.zh: 社区不需要等到灾难正在形成时才开始准备。现有的社区应急计划、患者外展计划和社交网络为帮助的步骤提供了起点。

paragraphs.en: First, communities can identify where disruptions could become public health emergencies.
paragraphs.zh: 首先，社区可以确定哪些干扰可能成为公共卫生紧急情况。

paragraphs.en: State departments of health and other social services can combine regional weather outlooks with local information about areas facing the highest risks, including the health impacts of water exposure on homes, guidance for avoiding polluted floodwaters and evacuation routes.
paragraphs.zh: 国家卫生部门和其他社会服务部门可以将区域天气展望联合收割机与面临最高风险地区的当地信息结合起来，包括水暴露对房屋的健康影响，避免污染洪水的指导和疏散路线。

paragraphs.en: Community organizations can help identify individuals and neighborhoods that may face language barriers and ensure they receive lifesaving alerts and information they can understand.
paragraphs.zh: 社区组织可以帮助识别可能面临语言障碍的个人和社区，并确保他们收到救生警报和他们可以理解的信息。

paragraphs.en: Second, it’s important to protect continuity of clinical care for patients during disasters.
paragraphs.zh: 第二，重要的是在灾害期间保护患者临床护理的连续性。

paragraphs.en: Health systems and public health departments can coordinate with health providers in hospitals, pharmacies and home health services to identify people who depend on regular medical appointments or transportation and ensure they can still receive care.
paragraphs.zh: 卫生系统和公共卫生部门可以与医院、药店和家庭保健服务机构的保健提供者协调，以确定依赖定期医疗预约或交通的人，并确保他们仍然可以得到护理。

paragraphs.en: In practice, this may be providing flexible scheduling options, organizing alternative means of transportation or identifying alternative care locations that may be more accessible.
paragraphs.zh: 在实践中，这可能是提供灵活的时间安排选择，组织替代交通工具或确定可能更方便的替代护理地点。

paragraphs.en: Third, weather warnings can be most useful when they provide information people can act on, such as where to find food, transportation or mental health support.
paragraphs.zh: 第三，天气警报在提供人们可以采取行动的信息时最有用，例如在哪里可以找到食物，交通或心理健康支持。

paragraphs.en: Many local and state emergency services already work to educate the public about storm risks ahead. They can do more by also telling residents where they can find safe water and food, how to limit exposure to chemicals or disease vectors, how to store medicine safely, and whom to contact for transportation, shelter or mental health support.
paragraphs.zh: 许多地方和州的紧急服务机构已经在努力教育公众有关未来的风暴风险。他们可以做得更多，还可以告诉居民在哪里可以找到安全的水和食物，如何限制接触化学品或疾病媒介，如何安全地储存药品，以及联系谁来获得交通，住所或心理健康支持。

paragraphs.en: Information that is specific enough to use and relevant to the community can save lives.
paragraphs.zh: 足够具体、可供使用且与社区相关的信息可以拯救生命。

paragraphs.en: Preparation is preventive care
paragraphs.zh: 准备是预防性护理

paragraphs.en: Because signs of the coming weather shift can be detected months in advance, El Niño forecasts offer something that immediate storm forecasts can’t: extra time to identify these health risks, secure medical care for the months ahead and prepare so warnings are useful to residents.
paragraphs.zh: 由于即将到来的天气变化的迹象可以提前几个月检测到，厄尔尼诺预报提供了即时风暴预报无法提供的东西：额外的时间来识别这些健康风险，确保未来几个月的医疗保健，并准备好对居民有用的警告。

paragraphs.en: When warnings pair information about the risk with practical actions and local resources, they can empower people rather than leaving them feeling helpless in the face of a disaster.
paragraphs.zh: 当警告将有关风险的信息与实际行动和当地资源结合起来时，它们可以增强人们的力量，而不是让他们在灾难面前感到无助。
